Self-regulated learning scores simulated by a large language model

Source: R/data.R
srl.Rd

Scores on five constructs of the Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire (MSLQ) for 300 simulated respondents. Each score is the mean of the construct's Likert items, on a scale from 1 to 7. The responses were generated by a large language model (GPT), not collected from students: they come from a study of how language models answer psychological surveys, and are used here because they are a well-structured, openly shareable cross-sectional example. They should not be read as evidence about students.

Usage

srl

Format

A data frame with 300 rows and 5 columns:

cognitive_strategies

cognitive strategy use

intrinsic_value

intrinsic value of the course

self_efficacy

self-efficacy

self_regulation

self-regulation

test_anxiety

test anxiety

Source

The SRL_GPT data of the psychnets package, with descriptive column names. Saqr, M. (2025). Delving into the psychology of machines: Exploring the structure of self-regulated learning via LLM-generated survey responses. Computers in Human Behavior, 173, 108769. doi:10.1016/j.chb.2025.108769

Details

The five constructs are strongly correlated (about 0.8, except test anxiety), which makes the data a good illustration of how the choice of covariance structure shapes a latent profile analysis.

Examples

descriptives(srl, names(srl))
#>               variable   n n_missing     mean        sd      min      max
#> 1 cognitive_strategies 300         0 5.707179 0.5408047 4.153846 7.000000
#> 2      intrinsic_value 300         0 6.116296 0.5226347 4.222222 7.000000
#> 3        self_efficacy 300         0 5.926296 0.5870661 4.000000 7.000000
#> 4      self_regulation 300         0 5.544074 0.5000432 3.777778 6.777778
#> 5         test_anxiety 300         0 3.700000 0.6443088 2.000000 5.750000
#>   n_distinct
#> 1         34
#> 2         22
#> 3         25
#> 4         25
#> 5         16
